name: Brookfield Asset Management Ltd.
headquarters: Brookfield Place, 225 Liberty Street, New York, NY, United States
founded: Incorporated 2022; the Brookfield franchise claims over 125 years of operating history
employees: Over 5,800 investment and asset-management professionals (over 60% in the US after the Oaktree completion); about 250,000 operating employees across the managed businesses
summary:
**BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:** This dossier's subject is **Brookfield Asset Management Ltd. (NYSE/TSX: BAM)** — the listed asset manager — and not Brookfield Corporation, Brookfield Infrastructure or Brookfield Renewable, because BAM is where the AI-infrastructure deals are actually executed. Every marquee announcement in this corpus's period (the USD 100bn AI infrastructure programme with NVIDIA and the Kuwait Investment Authority, France, Sweden, Qatar, Korea, Paducah and Aypa Power) is published under BAM's name and deployed through BAM-managed funds. BAM is also the only entity in the complex filing US-domestic forms.

**BACKGROUND.** BAM holds **100% of Brookfield's asset-management business** following the 2025 Arrangement of 4 February 2025, in which Brookfield Corporation transferred its roughly 73% interest in that business to BAM for newly issued Class A shares. Fee-bearing capital **USD 602,714m at 31 December 2025** and **USD 672bn at 30 June 2026** (+19% year on year), against total AUM the firm states as 'over USD 1 trillion'. FY2025 revenues USD 4,817m and net income USD 2,398m under US GAAP.

**The structure is the subject.** BAM is a fee-and-carry entity with a deliberately small balance sheet — total assets USD 20,080m at 30 June 2026 against Brookfield Corporation's USD 525,515m. Its listed affiliates BIP and BEP are **minority co-investors** in the deals BAM's funds lead, and a dossier written around either would understate the figures by 80-90%: BIP holds about **15% of Compass Datacenters**, equity-accounted, and BEP took about USD 420m of Aypa's roughly USD 3bn equity cheque.
ecosystemRole: We assess Brookfield as the ecosystem's most operationally integrated investor — the one that owns generation, transmission-adjacent assets and data-centre platforms inside a single franchise and can therefore offer a 'bring-your-own-power' proposition that a pure financial sponsor cannot. The Paducah campus is the clearest expression: Brookfield assembled a consortium with NextEra and three local utilities to build up to 1.8 GW of utility capacity and over 1.2 GW of compute at a US Department of Energy site. For vendors in this corpus, Brookfield is reached through Compass, Data4, Ascenty and Csquare on the data-centre side and through Brookfield Renewable on the power side, and — as with Blackstone — it appears in supplier dossiers as an ownership attribution rather than as a direct counterparty.

productsAndServices.name: Infrastructure
productsAndServices.description: USD 247bn of AUM and USD 106,398m of fee-bearing capital at 31 December 2025; about 230 investment professionals and about 64,000 operating employees. Brookfield's own framing covers utilities, transport, midstream and data infrastructure — the last defined as 'businesses that provide essential services and critical infrastructure to transmit and store data globally, including telecom towers and active rooftop sites, fiber optic cable and data centers'.
highlights: Brookfield Infrastructure Fund (BIF) flagship series — the sixth vintage raised USD 9.3bn in Q2 2026 alone and is expected to be the largest in the series; BIF V holds Compass

Brookfield AI Infrastructure Fund (BAIIF) — launched 19 November 2025 with a USD 10bn equity target, USD 5bn committed at launch from Brookfield, NVIDIA and the Kuwait Investment Authority; first close held in Q2 2026 at USD 5bn
Brookfield Infrastructure Structured Solutions (BISS) — inaugural vintage closed 11 March 2025 at about USD 1bn
Brookfield Infrastructure Debt Fund IV — first close over USD 4bn announced 1 October 2025
BIP, the listed perpetual vehicle, with USD 128.2bn of total assets at 31 December 2025 and a USD 29.2bn market capitalisation
productsAndServices.positioning: Infrastructure Investor's 2026 edition ranks Brookfield **third at USD 99.1bn** of five-year infrastructure fundraising, behind BlackRock (USD 113.4bn) and KKR (USD 100.5bn) and ahead of Macquarie (USD 87.9bn) and Blackstone (USD 45.7bn). Brookfield raises roughly twice as much infrastructure capital as Blackstone and about 13% more than Macquarie on this measure — but IPE Real Assets' AUM table for the prior year put **Macquarie first and Brookfield second**, both above USD 300bn. The two rankings measure flow and stock respectively and nothing reconciles them; both are carried.

productsAndServices.name: Renewable Power & Transition (marketed as 'Energy')
productsAndServices.description: USD 143bn of AUM and USD 67,245m of fee-bearing capital at 31 December 2025; about 175 investment professionals and about 20,100 operating employees. Hydro, utility-scale solar, wind, distributed energy and battery storage, plus 'sustainable solutions' including the Westinghouse nuclear-services stake held with Cameco.
highlights: Brookfield Global Transition Fund II — final institutional close 7 October 2025 at USD 20bn plus about USD 3.5bn of co-investment, roughly USD 23.5bn for the vintage. This is the fund acquiring Aypa Power
Microsoft renewable energy framework agreement — over 10.5 GW of new capacity between 2026 and 2030 in the US and Europe, announced 1 May 2024 and filed as a BEP exhibit

Google Hydro Framework Agreement — up to 3,000 MW of carbon-free hydroelectric capacity across the US, announced 15 July 2025, with Holtwood and Safe Harbor in Pennsylvania the first contracts at more than USD 3bn and 670 MW on 20-year power purchase agreements
Westinghouse — the US Department of Energy committed USD 17.5bn of conditional loan facilities for long-lead equipment for up to ten AP1000 reactors
BEP delivered about 3,100 MW of new capacity in the first half of 2026 and targets about 10,000 MW a year by 2027
productsAndServices.positioning: The Microsoft framework is the largest corporate renewable agreement in the corpus by nameplate, and the Google hydro agreement is described by the parties as the world's largest corporate clean-power deal for hydroelectricity. Both are frameworks rather than delivered capacity: the Microsoft build window **starts** in 2026, and no party publishes a contracted-or-delivered figure against the 10.5 GW. Notably, Microsoft's own SEC filings contain no full-text mention of Brookfield outside incidental benefit-plan filings.

productsAndServices.roadmap: BEP is guiding to about 10,000 MW of new projects a year by 2027, having signed power purchase agreements for about 2,600 MW of advanced-pipeline projects in Q2 2026.

productsAndServices.name: Data-centre platforms
productsAndServices.description: Brookfield's data-centre exposure runs through five named platforms held at minority, equity-accounted interests by BIP, alongside the funds BAM manages. The distinction between the platform's scale and Brookfield's interest in it is the thing most often lost.
highlights: Compass Datacenters — US, Canada, Israel and Italy; BIP holds an approximate 15% interest acquired 3 October 2023 for about USD 400m, carried as an equity-accounted investment in associate
Data4 — European hyperscale, over 30 data centres; BIP's effective interest about 18-19%; a 90% interest in a portfolio of stabilised assets was sold in Q3 2025 for about USD 1.7bn total
Ascenty — Latin America, a joint venture with Digital Realty; BIP's associate interest 12%
Digital Connexion — India, with Digital Realty and Reliance Jio; BIP's associate interest 8%

productsAndServices.positioning: Two first-party capacity figures exist with different scopes and must not be merged. Brookfield's group-level page states that Compass and Data4 together support 'more than 1.6 GW of contracted capacity and over 3.5 GW of development potential' — and carries **no publication date**. BIP's FY2025 Form 20-F states its own portfolio at 'over 150 operational data centers, with approximately 1.2 gigawatts of critical load capacity and 1.1 gigawatts of contracted capacity that will be built out' as at 31 December 2025. The first is a platform figure, the second is BIP's portfolio. **No independent ranking of data-centre owners exists** against which either could be placed.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Not sold directly; Brookfield's exposure is through fund and affiliate interests in the platforms.
targetSegments: Hyperscalers and cloud-service providers, via the platforms

strategyRead: **(High confidence)** We assess that **the entity question is the single most consequential fact about Brookfield in this corpus, and that BAM is the right answer**. Basis: every AI-infrastructure announcement in the period is published under BAM's name and deployed through BAM-managed funds (BAIIF, BIF VI, BGTF II); BAM is the only entity in the complex filing US-domestic forms; and BIP and BEP are minority co-investors, holding about 15% of Compass and about USD 420m of Aypa's roughly USD 3bn equity respectively. A dossier written around BIP or BEP would understate every figure by 80-90%; one written around BN would describe a USD 525bn balance sheet dominated by insurance float and consolidated operating assets.

**(High confidence)** We assess that **the 'Brookfield owns Compass' formulation fails, and the corrected version is more interesting than the error**. BIP acquired an approximate 15% interest on 3 October 2023 for about USD 400m, carried as an equity-accounted investment in an associate rather than consolidated. Ontario Teachers' — the pre-existing investor — used the phrase 'co-controlling shareholder' in its own release, and co-control sits with Brookfield-managed funds alongside it. The 2023 deal value is itself unreconciled across three incompatible figures (about USD 5.5bn and USD 5.7bn as platform valuations against USD 1.35-1.4bn as the stake consideration), and BIP's own Q2 2023 letter states USD 1.35bn 'including Brookfield Infrastructure's equity of approximately $375 million'. Every one of those numbers is a different thing.

**(High confidence)** We assess that **the USD 100bn AI figure is an asset-acquisition ambition and not a fund, and that the distinction is routinely lost**. BAIIF targets USD 10bn of equity and had USD 5bn committed at first close, including Brookfield's own money alongside NVIDIA's and the Kuwait Investment Authority's. The USD 100bn is what the programme intends to acquire once co-investment and leverage are applied. Reporting the fund at USD 100bn overstates it by an order of magnitude.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that **Brookfield's sovereign-AI programmes are commitments to a framework rather than to capacity, and that none of them has yet been shown to convert**. France (€20bn, later €30bn), Sweden (SEK 95bn), Qatar (USD 20bn) and Korea (up to USD 9bn) share a shape: a government or state fund supplies demand and siting, Brookfield supplies capital, and the announcement precedes the build by years. The Korea arrangement is described by NVIDIA as a non-binding term sheet; the France upsize from €20bn to €30bn appears only as a line in an earnings release with no standalone announcement located. The judgment is moderate because the pattern is clear but no completion data exists yet for any of them.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that **the Microsoft 10.5 GW framework is materially undelivered and that no party publishes the figure that would settle it**. The agreement dates from 1 May 2024 and its build window covers 2026 to 2030 — it has only just opened. No contracted-or-delivered megawatt figure against the 10.5 GW has been published by either party, and Microsoft's own SEC filings contain no full-text mention of Brookfield outside incidental benefit-plan filings. A reader treating 10.5 GW as installed capacity would be wrong by an unknown but large margin.

**(High confidence)** We assess that **BAM earns the fees while its parent keeps most of the carry, and that this is the structural difference from Blackstone**. Under the Relationship Agreement, Brookfield Corporation retains an economic interest equal to effectively 100% of carried interest earned in mature funds and 33.3% on newer ones. At Blackstone the listed parent is the manager and keeps its own carry. So two firms that look like peers on a league table have opposite answers to the question of who owns the upside — and BAM's FY2025 net income jump from USD 541m to USD 2,398m is largely the 2025 Arrangement restating ownership, not operations improving fourfold.

**Collection gap, stated:** no Brookfield entity had published a Q3 2026 earnings date as of 6 September 2026. The only forward items on the investor calendars are a Brookfield Investor Day on 17 September 2026 in New York and a BIP/BEP Investor Day on 29 September 2026 in Toronto. Every Q3 date carried in this dossier's refresh calendar is a cadence inference from the 2025 actuals and is labelled as such. Separately, no first-party source states a founding year for the franchise; the '125 years' framing comes from Brookfield's own capability page and is carried as the company's wording rather than as a date.

policyExposure.regime: Senate Banking Committee oversight — data-centre ownership and retail electricity prices
policyExposure.exposure: Brookfield Infrastructure Partners was one of four addressees — with Blackstone, BlackRock and KKR — of letters from the minority of the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs seeking documentation of efforts to mitigate the regulatory risks of owning data centres and an explanation of how a significant footprint in both energy supply and demand will not raise costs for consumers. Brookfield is exposed to the framing through a single franchise that owns generation (Brookfield Renewable's hydro fleet, the Westinghouse stake) and data-centre demand (Compass, Data4, Ascenty, Csquare).
policyExposure.mitigation: No published Brookfield response to the letters was located.

policyExposure.regime: US Department of Energy support for Westinghouse AP1000 deployment
policyExposure.exposure: The Department of Energy committed USD 17.5bn in conditional loan facilities to finance long-lead equipment for up to ten large-scale Westinghouse AP1000 reactors in the United States. Separately, under an October 2025 agreement between Brookfield, Cameco and the US Government, a contingent profit interest in Westinghouse vests for the Government once it makes a final investment decision and enters definitive agreements for new Westinghouse reactors with an aggregate value of at least USD 80bn before January 2029, in exchange for the Government arranging financing and facilitating permitting.
policyExposure.mitigation: Westinghouse is held through Brookfield Renewable's sustainable-solutions segment and co-owned with Cameco, so the exposure is shared rather than borne by BAM alone.

relationships.note: Brookfield-managed funds co-control Compass with Ontario Teachers'; BIP itself holds an approximate 15% equity-accounted interest.
relationships.context:
Brookfield Infrastructure and Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan agreed on 20 June 2023 to acquire Compass Datacenters from RedBird Capital Partners and the Azrieli Group, closing 3 October 2023. Ontario Teachers', already an investor, described Brookfield in its own release as a 'co-controlling shareholder' — the counterparty's own word, and the reason 'owns' overstates it.

BIP's FY2025 Form 20-F is precise about BIP's own position: 'an approximate 15% interest in a North American hyperscale data center platform, for total consideration of approximately $400 million', carried at 15% at both 31 December 2025 and 31 December 2024 as an investment in an associate — equity-accounted, not consolidated. BIP's Q2 2023 letter puts the co-controlling stake at USD 1.35bn 'including Brookfield Infrastructure's equity of approximately $375 million', against a platform valuation reported elsewhere at about USD 5.5bn. Those are three different measures and no source reconciles them.

relationships.note: Brookfield Global Transition Fund II, alongside Brookfield Renewable, has agreed to acquire Aypa Power from Blackstone — signed, not closed.
relationships.context:
Announced 22 July 2026 at about USD 7bn enterprise value and USD 3bn of equity value, for a platform of about 6.5 GW operating, under construction and contracted, 95% contracted with an average remaining contract life of 17 years, a development pipeline above 20 GW and about 200 staff.

The acquiring vehicle is the second vintage of Brookfield's flagship global transition strategy, BGTF II, which closed in October 2025 at USD 20bn plus about USD 3.5bn of co-investment. Brookfield Renewable's share is stated two ways in its own documents — about USD 420m net in the results release and about USD 760m in the Q2 2026 management discussion — and both are carried as stated. **The transaction has not closed.** BEP's Q2 2026 interim financial statements, Note 22, say closing 'is expected to occur in the second half of 2026 and is subject to customary closing conditions'; no regulator is named, and no completion had been announced as of 6 September 2026.

relationships.note: Direct peers in infrastructure fundraising, and counterparties on the pending Aypa Power sale.
relationships.context: Infrastructure Investor's 2026 edition ranks Brookfield third at USD 99.1bn of five-year infrastructure fundraising against Blackstone's eighth at USD 45.7bn. The two transacted directly in July 2026, when BGTF II agreed to buy Aypa Power from Blackstone Energy Transition Partners, and both were named with four other firms in NVIDIA's August 2026 programme to mobilise over USD 500bn of third-party capital.

One measures flow and the other stock; nothing reconciles them and both are carried. The two also sit on opposite sides of the same asset class in this corpus — Brookfield holds its data-centre platforms through minority equity-accounted interests, Macquarie exited its largest at eight years.

relationships.scale: framework expanded from USD 5bn to USD 25bn of total capex
relationships.note: Bloom Energy supplies behind-the-meter fuel cells under a framework Brookfield describes as a seed AI-infrastructure investment for its AI fund.
relationships.context:
The original framework covered up to 1 GW of behind-the-meter power for data centres and AI factories at about USD 5bn, and Brookfield described it as 'a seed AI infrastructure investment for the Fund' when launching BAIIF. It was expanded fivefold to USD 25bn of total capex, confirmed independently in BIP's, BN's and BAM's Q2 2026 disclosures, and BIP increased its equity commitment in the same quarter.

**A figure worth carrying with the relationship:** Bloom Energy's own Form 8-K filings break out related-party revenue from the Brookfield joint venture at USD 574.2m in Q4 2025, USD 373.3m in Q1 2026 and USD 2.8m in Q2 2026 — a near-total collapse in what was a record revenue quarter for Bloom. The figure is audited and counterparty-disclosed, and it appears in none of Brookfield's own channels. No source located explains the fall.

relationships.note: Brookfield's relationship with Crusoe is a USD 750m credit facility, not an equity position.
relationships.context: Confirmed first-party as a credit facility. Typed `other` rather than `portfolio` for the same reason as Blackstone's lending relationships: a facility is not a holding, and recording it as one would misstate what Brookfield owns.

relationships.note: Brookfield is named among reported suitors for Blue Owl's STACK Asia-Pacific portfolio — a report, not a transaction.
relationships.context: Bloomberg-sourced reporting from June 2026 places Brookfield among reported bidders for STACK's Tokyo, Osaka, Sydney, Melbourne and Johor portfolio, alongside the AI Infrastructure Partnership, IFM, KKR and DigitalBridge, in a process that could exceed USD 30bn. No party has confirmed. Typed `other` because a reported interest is not an ownership, customer or supplier relationship, and recorded here only so a reader of STACK's dossier can see the claim has been checked from this side and remains unconfirmed.

metrics.result: The pre-Arrangement figure: BAM then held about 27% of the asset-management business.

periods.commentary: BAM became a US domestic filer only from FY2024; it filed Form 20-F for FY2022 and Form 40-F for FY2023, so the comparative series changes reporting regime twice in three years.

metrics.name: Net income attributable to BAM
metrics.result: Up from USD 541m — but the step is substantially the 2025 Arrangement giving BAM 100% of the asset-management business rather than a fourfold operating improvement. Total profit (before the attribution split) was USD 2,108m in FY2024 and USD 2,398m in FY2025, and those two figures converging is the tell.

financials.commentary: All four listed Brookfield entities report in US dollars — BAM under US GAAP, BN and the partnerships under IFRS. Figures here are BAM's unless stated. **A caution about a widely-circulated miss:** Brookfield Corporation's Q2 2026 headline of USD 0.14 against a USD 0.65 consensus appears to be a data-provider mapping artefact — the same feed showed a revenue consensus of USD 1.67bn against USD 19.41bn actual, and the shares moved less than 1% — so it is not carried as a result.
